title: Regression Analysis
curriculum_locator: Stat H-303 Regression Analysis & Stat H-312 Regression Lab; University of Dhaka four-year B.S. Honours Statistics curriculum, starting session 2023–2024

units.title: Simple Linear Regression: OLS Estimation, Gauss-Markov Theorem, Normal Equations & ANOVA Decomposition
scope: Conditional expectation functions E[Y | X = x], population regression lines, and the classical Gauss-Markov assumptions
Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) derivation of slope beta_1_hat and intercept beta_0_hat; algebraic orthogonality properties of OLS residuals
Sampling distributions, unbiasedness, variances, and covariance of OLS estimators; unbiased estimation of error variance s^2 = SSE / (n - 2)
Proof of the Gauss-Markov Theorem (BLUE property) in the bivariate case and equivalence with Maximum Likelihood under normal errors
Partitioning Total Sum of Squares (SST = SSR + SSE), coefficient of determination R^2, ANOVA F-test, andWorking-Hotelling confidence bands vs prediction intervals

units.title: Multiple Linear Regression in Matrix Form: Orthogonal Projections, Hat Matrix & Partial Correlations
scope: Matrix formulation of the general linear model Y = X beta + epsilon, rank conditions, and normal equations (X^T X) beta_hat = X^T Y
Geometric interpretation of OLS: column space Col(X), orthogonal projection matrix (Hat matrix) H = X(X^T X)^(-1)X^T, and idempotency of H and I - H
Expectation vector E[beta_hat] = beta, variance-covariance matrix Var(beta_hat) = sigma^2 (X^T X)^(-1), and Matrix Gauss-Markov Theorem (Loewner positive semi-definite ordering)
Quadratic forms of normal random vectors, Cochran's Theorem, independence of beta_hat and SSE, and unbiasedness of s^2 = Y^T(I - H)Y / (n - p)
Frisch-Waugh-Lovell (FWL) Theorem, partial regression coefficients, sequential (Type I) vs partial (Type III) sums of squares, partial R^2, and adjusted R_a^2

units.title: Exact & Asymptotic Inference in Linear Models: General Linear Hypotheses, Confidence Ellipsoids & Simultaneous Intervals
scope: General Linear Hypothesis testing H_0: C beta = d where C is a full-row-rank q x p contrast matrix
Full vs Reduced model sum-of-squares principle and derivation of the exact F-statistic F = ((SSE_R - SSE_F)/q) / (SSE_F/(n - p))
Individual coefficient t-tests, linear combinations c^T beta, and testing equality or structural restrictions across regression parameters
Joint 100(1 - alpha)% confidence ellipsoids for beta, Bonferroni simultaneous intervals, and Scheffé's S-method for all linear contrasts
Confidence intervals for mean response E[Y | x_0] = x_0^T beta and prediction intervals for future observations Y_new at x_0

units.title: Regression Diagnostics, Leverage & Influence Analysis: Studentized Residuals, Cook's Distance & DFFITS
scope: Hat matrix diagonals h_ii (leverage): bounds 1/n <= h_ii <= 1, average leverage p/n, and Mahalanobis distance interpretation in predictor space
Raw residuals e_i, internally studentized residuals r_i, and leave-one-out deletion (PRESS) residuals e_(i) = e_i / (1 - h_ii)
Externally studentized (jackknife / R-student) residuals t_i, exact Student t_(n-p-1) distribution, and Bonferroni outlier testing
Influence diagnostics via Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury rank-one updates: Cook's Distance D_i, DFFITS_i, DFBETAS_j(i), and COVRATIO_i
Graphical diagnostics: Normal Q-Q plots, residual-vs-fitted fan patterns, Added-Variable (partial regression) plots, and Component-Plus-Residual (partial residual) plots

units.title: Violations of Classical Assumptions: Heteroscedasticity, Weighted Least Squares, GLS & Autocorrelation
scope: Nonspherical error covariance Var(epsilon) = sigma^2 Omega: inefficiency of OLS and bias of standard OLS covariance estimators
Aitken's Generalized Least Squares (GLS) estimator beta_GLS = (X^T Omega^(-1) X)^(-1) X^T Omega^(-1) Y and Weighted Least Squares (WLS) for heteroscedastic variances
Detecting heteroscedasticity: Breusch-Pagan / Godfrey LM test, White's general test, Goldfeld-Quandt test, and Glejser/Park tests
Heteroscedasticity-Consistent (HC0, HC1, HC2, HC3) Huber-Eicker-White sandwich standard errors
First-order autoregressive AR(1) disturbances epsilon_t = rho epsilon_(t-1) + u_t: Durbin-Watson d-test, Breusch-Godfrey test, Prais-Winsten, and Cochrane-Orcutt iterative FGLS

units.title: Multicollinearity, Variance Inflation, Regularized Shrinkage (Ridge & LASSO) & Dimension Reduction
scope: Exact versus near multicollinearity: geometry of ill-conditioned X^T X matrices, determinant collapse, and variance inflation
Diagnostic metrics for multicollinearity: Variance Inflation Factor VIF_j = 1 / (1 - R_j^2), tolerance, spectral condition number kappa(X), and Belsley-Kuh-Welsch variance decomposition proportions
Tikhonov regularization and Hoerl-Kennard Ridge Regression: beta_ridge(lambda) = (X^T X + lambda I)^(-1) X^T Y, bias-variance trade-off, and existence theorem
Tibshirani's LASSO (L_1 penalty), subgradient KKT optimality conditions, soft-thresholding operator, variable selection sparsity, and Elastic Net
Principal Component Regression (PCR), Partial Least Squares (PLS), and K-fold Cross-Validation / Generalized Cross-Validation (GCV) for tuning lambda

units.title: Qualitative Predictors, Interaction Effects, Structural Breaks, Polynomial Splines & Model Selection
scope: Dummy (indicator) variables for categorical factors, reference cell vs effects coding, and avoidance of the Dummy Variable Trap
Interaction terms between continuous and categorical predictors, Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA), and Chow Test for structural stability across regimes
Polynomial regression, ill-conditioning of Vandermonde power bases, Forsythe orthogonal polynomials, piecewise linear segmented regression, and cubic B-splines
Variance-stabilizing and linearizing transformations: Box-Cox power family y^(lambda) and profile log-likelihood estimation of lambda
Variable selection and information criteria: Adjusted R^2, Mallows' C_p, PRESS statistic, Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), and stepwise/all-subsets algorithms

units.title: Nonlinear Regression, Robust Regression & Generalized Linear Models (Logistic & Poisson)
scope: Intrinsically nonlinear regression models Y_i = f(x_i, theta) + epsilon_i (Michaelis-Menten, Gompertz, logistic growth, exponential decay)
Nonlinear Least Squares (NLS) optimization: Gauss-Newton Taylor linearization, Levenberg-Marquardt damping, and asymptotic covariance sigma^2 (J^T J)^(-1)
Robust regression for heavy-tailed contamination: L_1 Least Absolute Deviations (LAD), Huber M-estimation, Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (IRLS), and Tukey's biweight
Generalized Linear Models (GLMs): exponential dispersion family, linear predictor eta = X beta, canonical link functions g(mu), and Fisher Scoring / IRLS
Binary Logistic Regression (logit link, odds ratios, Wald/deviance tests, Hosmer-Lemeshow) and Poisson Log-Linear Regression for count data and overdispersion
